fragments.text: Good morning, good afternoon, good evening. My name is Shabika Isaacs and I am a professor at the University of Johannesburg. And I also serve as an independent digital learning specialist also working in the field of AI and education. And so today I want to talk about the idea of a critical human agency in relation to the rapid emergence and evolution of generative AI. And I'm encouraged and inspired by the slogan that UNESCO had adopted when it launched its global education monitoring reports in August this year. And they launched it in the name of a campaign entitled Tech on Outterms. And I think behind that lies the notion of our as being human technology on the terms of us as human beings.
fragments.summary: My name is Shabika Isaacs and I am a professor at the University of Johannesburg.

fragments.text: But also we recognize that as human beings everyone isn't equal. And so we also want to design and apply and integrate in our society, in our economy and in our various sectors, technologies on the terms that would be beneficial for humans everywhere, for all human beings, especially those who are most marginalized and excluded. And this is the focus of my talk today. So I think the first thing to recognize is the emergence of generative AI in the public domain. It has in fact been grounded in controversy and contestation. And that's where it becomes imperative for us to name those contestations and controversies so that we can come to terms with what it means
fragments.summary: But also we recognize that as human beings everyone isn't equal.
